role: Former Governor of Florida; U.S. Senator
bio: Lawton Chiles walked 1,000 miles across Florida to win his 1970 Senate race, served three terms, chaired the Budget Committee, and returned as governor from 1991 to 1998, where he won the state's landmark tobacco settlement.

signatureStances.blurb: Won Florida's 1997 tobacco settlement and expanded children's health coverage.
signatureStances.quote: State of Florida tobacco Master Settlement (1997).

name: Reubin Askew
bio: Reubin Askew was governor of Florida from 1971 to 1979, a 'New South' reformer who pushed corporate taxation, court and disclosure reforms, and school desegregation, and briefly ran for president in 1984.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Bill Nelson
bio: Bill Nelson represented Florida in the U.S. House and then the Senate from 2001 to 2019, flew aboard the Space Shuttle in 1986, and served as NASA administrator from 2021 to 2025.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Marco Rubio
bio: Marco Rubio represented Florida in the U.S. Senate from 2011 to 2025, ran for president in 2016, was a China and Latin America hawk on the Intelligence and Foreign Relations committees, and became U.S. Secretary of State in 2025.

signatureStances.blurb: A leading China and Cuba hawk who co-wrote the forced-labor import ban.
signatureStances.quote: Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (S. 65, 117th Congress).

name: Claude Pepper
bio: Claude Pepper served Florida in the U.S. Senate from 1936 to 1951 and the House from 1963 to 1989, a New Deal liberal who in his later years was Congress's fiercest defender of Social Security and Medicare and an opponent of mandatory retirement.

signatureStances.blurb: Blocked benefit cuts and led the 1983 fight to save Social Security; sponsored the end of mandatory retirement.
signatureStances.quote: Sponsored the 1986 amendments to the Age Discrimination in Employment Act that abolished most mandatory retirement ages.

name: Mike DeWine
bio: Mike DeWine is governor of Ohio, a former U.S. senator, attorney general, and lieutenant governor; his long career blends social conservatism with breaks from his party on gun background checks and the pandemic response.

signatureStances.blurb: After the 2019 Dayton shooting, proposed background-check and red-flag laws his own legislature rejected.
signatureStances.quote: 'STRONG Ohio' plan (Ohio SB 221, 133rd General Assembly, 2019).

name: Jim Tressel
bio: Jim Tressel is Ohio's lieutenant governor, appointed in 2025; he won a national championship as Ohio State's football coach and later served as president of Youngstown State University, and has focused on workforce training.
officeHistory: Head Football Coach, Ohio State University (2001-2010)

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Dave Yost
bio: Dave Yost is Ohio's attorney general; a former state auditor and county prosecutor, he explored a 2026 run for governor but ended his campaign in 2025 after the state party backed Vivek Ramaswamy. He has sued opioid distributors and the Biden administration and defended Ohio's abortion restrictions before voters overrode them via a 2023 ballot measure.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Frank LaRose
bio: Frank LaRose is Ohio's secretary of state, a former Army Green Beret and state senator; he ran the 2023 campaign to raise the threshold for citizen ballot initiatives to 60 percent, which voters rejected.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Rob McColley
bio: Rob McColley is president of the Ohio Senate, a lawyer from rural Napoleon in the state's northwest; he has pushed energy deregulation, income-tax cuts, and property-tax relief.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Matt Huffman
role: Speaker of the Ohio House of Representatives
bio: Matt Huffman is speaker of the Ohio House, an unusual move after serving as Senate president; a Lima lawyer, he is the architect of Ohio's private-school voucher expansion and a hardline negotiator on the budget.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Jim Jordan
bio: Jim Jordan chairs the House Judiciary Committee, co-founded the Freedom Caucus, and is one of the most confrontational Republicans in Congress on investigations of the Justice Department, the FBI, and technology companies.

signatureStances.blurb: A founding Freedom Caucus member who has voted against nearly every bipartisan spending deal.
signatureStances.quote: Co-founder, House Freedom Caucus (2015).

name: Marcy Kaptur
bio: Marcy Kaptur represents the Toledo-to-Cleveland lakeshore and is the longest-serving woman in the history of the U.S. House; an appropriator, she is a protectionist on trade and a champion of Great Lakes restoration.

signatureStances.blurb: A leading House opponent of NAFTA and permanent normal trade relations with China.
signatureStances.quote: Voted against NAFTA (1993) and against permanent normal trade relations with China (2000).

name: Mike Turner
bio: Mike Turner represents the Dayton area, is a former mayor of Dayton, and chaired the House Intelligence Committee until early 2025; he is a NATO and Ukraine hawk who has clashed with the isolationist wing of his party.

signatureStances.blurb: A NATO Parliamentary Assembly leader and consistent vote for Ukraine aid.
signatureStances.quote: Whipped Republican votes for the 2024 National Security Supplemental (H.R. 815, 118th Congress).

name: Dave Joyce
bio: Dave Joyce represents Cleveland's eastern exurbs, chairs an appropriations subcommittee, leads the centrist Republican Governance Group, and sponsors bipartisan cannabis-federalism legislation.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Emilia Sykes
bio: Emilia Sykes represents the Akron area and was previously the Democratic leader of the Ohio House; she focuses on maternal health, manufacturing, and infrastructure.
officeHistory: Ohio House of Representatives (2015-2022), Minority Leader (2019-2022)

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: John Kasich
bio: John Kasich chaired the House Budget Committee during the 1997 balanced-budget deal, hosted a Fox News show, and served two terms as governor of Ohio (2011-2019), where he expanded Medicaid over his own party's objections; he ran for president in 2000 and 2016.

signatureStances.blurb: Expanded Medicaid in Ohio under the Affordable Care Act, bypassing the legislature.
signatureStances.quote: Ohio Controlling Board approval of Medicaid expansion (October 2013).

signatureStances.blurb: Chief House negotiator of the deal that produced federal surpluses.
signatureStances.quote: Balanced Budget Act of 1997 (H.R. 2015, 105th Congress).

name: Sherrod Brown
bio: Sherrod Brown represented Ohio in the U.S. House and then the Senate from 2007 to 2025, when he narrowly lost re-election; a populist on trade and the 'dignity of work,' he chaired the Banking Committee.

signatureStances.blurb: A career-long trade protectionist who opposed NAFTA, CAFTA, and PNTR with China.
signatureStances.quote: Lead sponsor of legislation to penalize currency manipulation and 'Buy American' rules.

name: Rob Portman
bio: Rob Portman represented Ohio in the U.S. House and Senate (2011-2023) and served as U.S. Trade Representative and White House budget director; a deficit hawk and dealmaker, he co-wrote the 2021 bipartisan infrastructure law and came out for same-sex marriage in 2013.

signatureStances.blurb: Lead Republican negotiator of the 2021 bipartisan infrastructure law.
signatureStances.quote: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (H.R. 3684, 117th Congress).

name: John Glenn
bio: John Glenn was the first American to orbit the Earth in 1962 and represented Ohio in the U.S. Senate from 1974 to 1999, where he specialized in government operations and nuclear nonproliferation; in 1998 he returned to space aboard the Shuttle at age 77.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: John Boehner
bio: John Boehner of southwest Ohio was Speaker of the U.S. House from 2011 to 2015, leading a Republican majority repeatedly at odds with its own right flank over shutdowns and the debt ceiling; he resigned in 2015 and later joined a cannabis-industry board.

signatureStances.blurb: Co-authored the No Child Left Behind Act with George Miller and Ted Kennedy.
signatureStances.quote: No Child Left Behind Act of 2001 (H.R. 1, 107th Congress).

name: Dennis Kucinich
bio: Dennis Kucinich was the 'boy mayor' of Cleveland in the late 1970s and represented a Cleveland district in the U.S. House from 1997 to 2013; he ran for president twice on an antiwar, Medicare-for-All platform and proposed a cabinet-level Department of Peace.

signatureStances.blurb: Led House efforts to defund the Iraq War and introduced articles of impeachment over it.
signatureStances.quote: Voted against the Iraq War authorization (H.J.Res. 114, 107th Congress); sponsored a Department of Peace bill.

name: James Rhodes
bio: James Rhodes served four terms as governor of Ohio across three decades (1963-1971 and 1975-1983), campaigning relentlessly on 'jobs and progress' and industrial recruitment; he ordered the National Guard to Kent State University in 1970.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: JB Pritzker
bio: JB Pritzker, an heir to the Hyatt hotel fortune, is governor of Illinois; he has enacted a $15 minimum wage, recreational cannabis, abortion protections, and an assault-weapons ban, and is often mentioned as a 2028 presidential contender.

signatureStances.blurb: Signed Illinois's ban on the sale of assault weapons and high-capacity magazines.
signatureStances.quote: Protect Illinois Communities Act (Illinois Public Act 102-1116, 2023).

signatureStances.blurb: Signed the phase-in of a $15 statewide minimum wage.
signatureStances.quote: Illinois Public Act 101-1 (2019).

name: Kwame Raoul
bio: Kwame Raoul is Illinois's attorney general, elected to the state Senate seat once held by Barack Obama; he wrote the state's 2013 concealed-carry compromise and has led multistate litigation against the Trump administration.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Juliana Stratton
bio: Juliana Stratton is Illinois's lieutenant governor and won the 2026 Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate to succeed the retiring Dick Durbin; a former state representative from the South Side of Chicago, she has focused on criminal-justice reform and economic equity.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Alexi Giannoulias
bio: Alexi Giannoulias is Illinois's secretary of state, a former state treasurer who lost a 2010 Senate race to Mark Kirk; as secretary of state he has fought school library book bans and modernized the DMV.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Don Harmon
bio: Don Harmon is president of the Illinois Senate, a lawyer from Oak Park; he has steered pension, ethics, and revenue legislation and sponsored the constitutional amendment to replace the state's flat income tax with a graduated one, which voters rejected in 2020.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Chris Welch
role: Speaker of the Illinois House of Representatives
bio: Emanuel 'Chris' Welch is the first Black speaker of the Illinois House, elected in 2021 after the fall of Michael Madigan; a lawyer from the western Chicago suburbs, he has emphasized workers' rights and reproductive-health protections.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Raja Krishnamoorthi
bio: Raja Krishnamoorthi represents Chicago's northwest suburbs and is the top Democrat on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party; he ran for the 2026 Democratic U.S. Senate nomination and lost the primary to Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton.

signatureStances.blurb: Ranking member of the select committee on strategic competition with China.
signatureStances.quote: Ranking Member, House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party (118th-119th Congress).

name: Robin Kelly
bio: Robin Kelly represents a district from the South Side of Chicago into the rural south suburbs; she chaired the Democratic Party of Illinois and treats gun violence as a public-health crisis. She ran for the 2026 Democratic U.S. Senate nomination and finished third in the primary.

signatureStances.blurb: Publishes an annual 'Kelly Report' framing gun violence as a public-health emergency.
signatureStances.quote: Won her 2013 special election as the gun-control candidate after the Newtown shooting.

name: Jan Schakowsky
bio: Jan Schakowsky represents Evanston and Chicago's north lakefront; a member of Democratic leadership and the Progressive Caucus, she has pushed single-payer health care and consumer protection since 1999 and is not seeking re-election in 2026.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.

name: Chuy García
bio: Jesús 'Chuy' García represents a heavily Latino district drawn around the Chicago area; a former Cook County commissioner and 2015 mayoral candidate, he is a Progressive Caucus voice on immigration and transit.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Sean Casten
bio: Sean Casten represents Chicago's western suburbs; a former clean-energy company executive, he is one of the House's most technical voices on decarbonization and financial regulation of climate risk.

signatureStances.blurb: Ran a company that turned industrial waste heat into power before entering Congress.
signatureStances.quote: Sponsor of the Climate Risk Disclosure Act to require SEC climate reporting.

name: Lauren Underwood
bio: Lauren Underwood is a registered nurse who represents the far western suburbs of Chicago; she co-founded the Black Maternal Health Caucus and helped write the 2021 law that let states extend postpartum Medicaid.
officeHistory: Senior Advisor, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (2014-2016)

signatureStances.blurb: Lead author of the 'Momnibus' package on maternal mortality.
signatureStances.quote: Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act (H.R. 6142, 117th Congress).

name: Mike Bost
bio: Mike Bost represents the southern tip of Illinois, chairs the House Veterans' Affairs Committee, and is a former firefighter and Marine known for a 1995 floor tirade as a state legislator.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Mary Miller
bio: Mary Miller represents a large rural district in central and southern Illinois; a farmer and Freedom Caucus member, she is among the most socially conservative members of the House.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Everett Dirksen
bio: Everett Dirksen of Pekin was the Republican leader of the U.S. Senate from 1959 to 1969; his decision to deliver Republican votes was decisive in passing the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

signatureStances.blurb: Broke the Southern filibuster of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
signatureStances.quote: 'An idea whose time has come.' Delivered the Republican votes for cloture, June 10, 1964.

name: Paul Simon
bio: Paul Simon, recognizable by his bow tie and horn-rimmed glasses, represented Illinois in the U.S. House and Senate from 1985 to 1997, ran for president in 1988, and championed a balanced-budget amendment alongside liberal positions on most other issues.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Adlai Stevenson II
bio: Adlai Stevenson II was governor of Illinois from 1949 to 1953, twice the Democratic nominee for president against Eisenhower (1952 and 1956), and later ambassador to the United Nations during the Cuban Missile Crisis.
officeHistory: U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations (1961-1965)

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Carol Moseley Braun
bio: Carol Moseley Braun was the first Black woman elected to the U.S. Senate, representing Illinois from 1993 to 1999; she later served as ambassador to New Zealand and ran briefly for president in 2004.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Henry Hyde
bio: Henry Hyde represented Chicago's western suburbs from 1975 to 2007 and chaired the Judiciary and International Relations committees; his 1976 amendment barring federal Medicaid funding of abortion still governs federal policy, and he managed the 1998 impeachment of Bill Clinton.

signatureStances.blurb: Author of the standing ban on federal funding of abortion.
signatureStances.quote: Hyde Amendment, first attached to the FY1977 Labor-HEW appropriations bill in 1976 and renewed every year since.

name: Dan Rostenkowski
bio: Dan Rostenkowski, a product of the Chicago Democratic machine, chaired the House Ways and Means Committee from 1981 to 1994 and was a principal architect of the 1986 tax reform before a corruption conviction ended his career.
officeHistory: Chair, House Ways and Means Committee (1981-1994)

signatureStances.blurb: Co-authored the last major bipartisan overhaul of the federal tax code.
signatureStances.quote: Tax Reform Act of 1986 (H.R. 3838, 99th Congress).

name: Rod Blagojevich
bio: Rod Blagojevich was governor of Illinois from 2003 until his 2009 impeachment and removal for attempting to sell Barack Obama's vacated Senate seat; he was convicted on federal corruption charges and had his sentence commuted, and later pardoned, by Donald Trump.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Jim Thompson
bio: James 'Big Jim' Thompson was the longest-serving governor of Illinois (1977-1991); a former federal prosecutor who convicted a predecessor, he was a pragmatic Republican who worked closely with the Chicago Democratic organization and later chaired the 9/11 Commission's work in Illinois.
officeHistory: U.S. Attorney, Northern District of Illinois (1971-1975)

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Rahm Emanuel
bio: Rahm Emanuel was a Clinton and Obama White House official, chaired the House Democratic Caucus, served as mayor of Chicago from 2011 to 2019, and was U.S. ambassador to Japan from 2022 to 2025; he is a pugnacious centrist on fiscal and education policy.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Jesse Jackson
bio: Jesse Jackson, a protege of Martin Luther King Jr. based in Chicago, built the Rainbow/PUSH Coalition and ran for the Democratic presidential nomination in 1984 and 1988, expanding Black political participation and voter registration.
officeHistory: Founder, Operation PUSH (1971) and the Rainbow Coalition (1984)
Shadow U.S. Senator for the District of Columbia (1991-1997)

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Tim Walz
bio: Tim Walz, a former high-school teacher, football coach, and Army National Guard command sergeant major, represented a rural southern Minnesota district in Congress and has been governor since 2019; he was the Democratic nominee for vice president in 2024.

signatureStances.blurb: Signed universal free school meals and a paid family-leave program.
signatureStances.quote: Minnesota free school meals law and Paid Family and Medical Leave Act (2023).

signatureStances.blurb: Signed the PRO Act codifying a right to abortion in state law.
signatureStances.quote: Minnesota Protect Reproductive Options Act (2023).

name: Keith Ellison
bio: Keith Ellison was the first Muslim elected to Congress and a deputy chair of the Democratic National Committee before becoming Minnesota's attorney general in 2019; he personally led the prosecution that convicted Derek Chauvin for the murder of George Floyd.

signatureStances.blurb: Led the state prosecution team that convicted the officer who murdered George Floyd.
signatureStances.quote: State of Minnesota v. Derek Chauvin (2021).

name: Peggy Flanagan
bio: Peggy Flanagan is Minnesota's lieutenant governor and a member of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe, the second Native American woman elected to statewide executive office in U.S. history; she won the 2026 Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate.

name: Erin Murphy
role: Majority Leader of the Minnesota Senate
bio: Erin Murphy is the DFL majority leader of the Minnesota Senate, a nurse by training who ran for governor in 2018; she led the chamber through the 2023 session that enacted paid leave, abortion rights, cannabis legalization, and gun measures.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Lisa Demuth
role: Speaker of the Minnesota House of Representatives
bio: Lisa Demuth is speaker of the Minnesota House, the first Black person and first Republican woman to hold the office, representing a district around Cold Spring in central Minnesota; she is the 2026 Republican nominee for governor.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Tom Emmer
bio: Tom Emmer represents Minnesota's exurban and central district and is the House Majority Whip, the third-ranking Republican; a former state legislator and 2010 gubernatorial nominee, he is the party's leading voice on cryptocurrency.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Angie Craig
bio: Angie Craig represents Minnesota's competitive southern suburbs and is the top Democrat on the Agriculture Committee; a former medical-device executive, she ran for the 2026 Democratic U.S. Senate nomination and lost the primary to Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Betty McCollum
bio: Betty McCollum represents St. Paul and is the top Democrat on the defense appropriations subcommittee; she is a longtime advocate for Indian Country, public lands, and conditioning military aid on human rights.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Pete Stauber
bio: Pete Stauber represents northeastern Minnesota's Iron Range, a former professional hockey player and police officer; he chairs a Natural Resources subcommittee and is the leading congressional champion of copper-nickel mining near the Boundary Waters.
officeHistory: St. Louis County Board of Commissioners (2013-2019)

signatureStances.blurb: Lead sponsor of legislation to reverse the federal mineral withdrawal that blocks copper-nickel mining near the Boundary Waters.

name: Dean Phillips
bio: Dean Phillips, an heir to a distilling company and former Talenti gelato owner, represented Minnesota's affluent western suburbs from 2019 to 2025; a centrist, he mounted a long-shot primary challenge to President Biden in 2024 arguing Democrats needed a younger nominee.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Walter Mondale
bio: Walter Mondale was Minnesota's attorney general, a U.S. senator, and vice president under Jimmy Carter, redefining the vice presidency as a genuine governing partner; he was the 1984 Democratic presidential nominee and later ambassador to Japan.
officeHistory: Vice President of the United States (1977-1981)

signatureStances.blurb: Co-managed the Senate passage of the Fair Housing Act of 1968.
signatureStances.quote: Fair Housing Act, Title VIII of the Civil Rights Act of 1968 (H.R. 2516, 90th Congress).

name: Hubert Humphrey
bio: Hubert Humphrey, the 'Happy Warrior,' galvanized the 1948 Democratic convention with a speech demanding a civil-rights plank, served three decades in the Senate as a champion of civil rights and the Peace Corps, was Lyndon Johnson's vice president, and narrowly lost the 1968 presidential election.
officeHistory: Vice President of the United States (1965-1969)

signatureStances.blurb: Lead Senate sponsor of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and author of the 1948 convention plank.
signatureStances.quote: 'Get out of the shadow of states' rights and walk forthrightly into the bright sunshine of human rights.' (1948).

name: Eugene McCarthy
bio: Eugene McCarthy represented Minnesota in the U.S. House and Senate from 1949 to 1971; his antiwar challenge to President Johnson in the 1968 New Hampshire primary helped drive Johnson from the race.

signatureStances.blurb: His 1968 antiwar primary campaign made Vietnam a fault line inside the Democratic Party.

name: Paul Wellstone
bio: Paul Wellstone, a college professor and community organizer, won an upset Senate race in 1990 and became the leading progressive dissenter of his era, voting against welfare reform, the Defense of Marriage Act, and the Iraq War; he died in a plane crash days before the 2002 election.

signatureStances.blurb: Co-authored the federal mental-health parity law enacted after his death.
signatureStances.quote: Paul Wellstone and Pete Domenici Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act of 2008 (H.R. 1424).

name: Al Franken
bio: Al Franken, a 'Saturday Night Live' writer and performer and liberal talk-radio host, won a 2008 Senate recount by 312 votes and became a sharp Judiciary Committee questioner before resigning in 2017 amid misconduct allegations.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.

name: Norm Coleman
bio: Norm Coleman was the Democratic mayor of St. Paul who switched parties, won a 2002 Senate race after Paul Wellstone's death, lost the 2008 recount to Al Franken, and became a major Republican fundraiser and pro-Israel advocate.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Jesse Ventura
bio: Jesse Ventura, a former professional wrestler, Navy underwater demolition team member, and radio host, was elected governor of Minnesota in 1998 on the Reform Party ticket, the highest office ever won by a third-party candidate in modern times; he was fiscally conservative and socially libertarian.

signatureStances.blurb: Returned budget surpluses to taxpayers through 'Jesse checks' rebates.
signatureStances.quote: Minnesota sales-tax rebate checks (1999-2001).

name: Tim Pawlenty
bio: Tim Pawlenty was governor of Minnesota from 2003 to 2011, holding the line against tax increases with fees and accounting shifts, and ran briefly for the Republican presidential nomination in 2012.
officeHistory: Minnesota House of Representatives (1993-2003), Majority Leader (1999-2003)

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Michele Bachmann
bio: Michele Bachmann represented Minnesota's conservative outer suburbs from 2007 to 2015, founded the House Tea Party Caucus, and won the 2011 Ames Straw Poll before an early exit from the presidential race.

signatureStances.blurb: Founder and chair of the House Tea Party Caucus.
signatureStances.quote: Founded the Congressional Tea Party Caucus (2010).

name: Melissa Hortman
role: Former Speaker of the Minnesota House
bio: Melissa Hortman was speaker of the Minnesota House from 2019 until a February 2025 power-sharing deal made her Speaker Emerita and DFL leader; she was the chief legislative architect of the DFL's 2023 agenda on abortion, paid leave, gun safety, and climate. She and her husband, Mark, were shot and killed at their home in a targeted political attack on June 14, 2025.
officeHistory: Speaker Emerita and House DFL Leader (Feb-June 2025)

signatureStances.blurb: Steered the law committing Minnesota to 100% carbon-free electricity by 2040.
signatureStances.quote: Minnesota 100% Clean Energy by 2040 Act (2023).

name: Josh Shapiro
bio: Josh Shapiro is governor of Pennsylvania and a former state attorney general; a fast-talking moderate frequently mentioned as a future Democratic presidential contender, he survived an arson attack on the governor's residence in April 2025.

signatureStances.blurb: Struck permitting-overhaul deals with business groups and pushed a state PACT Act to speed approvals.
signatureStances.quote: Pennsylvania's 2024 permitting-reform executive order and RESET Board.

name: Austin Davis
bio: Austin Davis is Pennsylvania's lieutenant governor, the first Black person elected to the office; a former state representative and Allegheny County councilman from McKeesport.

name: Dave Sunday
bio: Dave Sunday is Pennsylvania's attorney general, a former York County district attorney who campaigned on fentanyl prosecution and won the only statewide row office Republicans held in 2024.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.

name: Stacy Garrity
bio: Stacy Garrity is Pennsylvania's state treasurer, an Army Reserve veteran and former corporate executive who pulled state investments from firms boycotting fossil-fuel and firearms companies.

name: Tim DeFoor
bio: Tim DeFoor is Pennsylvania's auditor general, a former Dauphin County controller and the first Republican elected to the office in nearly two decades; he audits state agencies and school and pension funds.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.

name: Joanna McClinton
bio: Joanna McClinton is speaker of the Pennsylvania House, the first woman and first Black person to hold the office; a former public defender from Philadelphia, she has led a chamber Democrats control by a single seat.

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Kim Ward
role: President pro tempore of the Pennsylvania Senate
bio: Kim Ward is president pro tempore of the Pennsylvania Senate, the first woman to hold the post; a Westmoreland County legislator, she has pushed election-law changes and opposed Governor Shapiro's spending priorities.
officeHistory: President pro tempore of the Pennsylvania Senate (2023-present)

signatureStances.blurb: District-focused economic priorities.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Brian Fitzpatrick
bio: Brian Fitzpatrick represents Bucks County, a former FBI agent who co-chairs the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus and is among the most frequent Republican defectors from party-line votes.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.

name: Scott Perry
bio: Scott Perry represents the Harrisburg area, a former Freedom Caucus chair whose phone was seized by the FBI in 2022 over his role pushing efforts to overturn the 2020 election.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.

name: Summer Lee
bio: Summer Lee represents Pittsburgh, the first Black woman Pennsylvania sent to Congress; a Squad-aligned progressive, she centers labor organizing and a Gaza cease-fire push.

name: Chrissy Houlahan
bio: Chrissy Houlahan represents Chester County, an Air Force veteran and former textile-company executive who serves on Armed Services and Foreign Affairs as a national-security-minded moderate.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Bob Casey Jr.
bio: Bob Casey Jr. represented Pennsylvania in the Senate from 2007 to 2025, the son of a governor and one of the chamber's few anti-abortion Democrats early in his career before shifting to support codifying Roe; he lost a razor-thin 2024 race to Dave McCormick.

signatureStances.blurb: Core fiscal and tax posture in the Senate.
Signature contrast on health and entitlements.

name: Rick Santorum
bio: Rick Santorum represented Pennsylvania in the House and Senate from 1991 to 2007, a social conservative who chaired the Senate Republican Conference before losing his 2006 re-election, and ran for president in 2012 and 2016.

signatureStances.blurb: Co-authored the 1996 federal welfare-reform overhaul.
signatureStances.quote: Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (H.R. 3734, 104th Congress).

name: Arlen Specter
